description: Jerez Monsalves and coauthors publish input tables for a Danish district-heating waste-heat policy study. The GitHub repository contains GAMS-ready generator, policy and other CSV files, configurable time-series folders, model-run outputs and scripts to extract result summaries. The describing Applied Energy paper evaluates operating or capital subsidies, carbon taxes and combinations under decarbonisation and consumer-cost limits. The repository README explains its directory structure and scenario flags, but exact CSV units and time step were not checked because payloads were not downloaded. It claims Apache-2.0 while its referenced LICENSE file is absent from the inspected tree; dataset reuse terms therefore need confirmation. Reading the tables is free, but rerunning the optimisation requires GAMS access. Geographic coverage is the study’s Denmark case, not a generic map of all Danish heat networks. A modeller could use the input structure to test alternative waste-heat availability or policy-cost scenarios after checking units and solver assumptions. Related catalogue resource data-district-heating-long-term-unit-commitment-instances provides a separate heat-system optimisation benchmark, not this policy input set.
